strategy.title: No plan settles inside 14 days
strategy.why: The only opening (three signed school-district bus-route accessibility audits at $3,000 each, $9,000 total) is established on every link except timing: school districts take 75 days to usable cash, and the window is 14 days, so none of the $6,000 settles in time.

alternatives.title: Deliver the three signed district audits anyway
alternatives.why: Worth doing for the money, but the $9,000 settles around day 75, far outside the 14-day window, so it contributes $0 to this goal.

steps.label: Ask whether the signed districts will pay on delivery or by card (shortening the 75-day settlement), and search for openings that settle within 14 days with no up-front capital

noPlan.decisiveGap: School districts' cash arrives 75 days after the sale; the goal's window is 14 days, so the signed $9,000 settles outside the deadline and no held opening brings any settled cash in time.
noPlan.resolution: Owner extends the deadline to at least 75 days (the signed audits then carry $9,000 against the $6,000 target), or Brain secures payment-on-delivery terms from the districts or finds an opening that settles within 14 days with no up-front capital.

excluded.why: Settles in 75 days against a 14-day window.

constraints.suggestion: Extend the window to at least 75 days, when the three signed district audits ($9,000) settle.

review.reasons: NO_PLAN with a DEADLINE constraint is correct. Three written acceptances at $3,000 ($9,000) are established on every link except settlement: the card records 75 days to usable cash against a 14-day window, so $0 settles in time, and no held opening can reach the $6,000 even with all evidence. Brain's own verdict agrees (move the deadline to 75 days or lower the target). The research step (payment-on-delivery terms, other openings) is appropriate.
findings: Minor: the resolution says that extending to 75 days makes the audits carry $9,000. It ignores the $25 direct cost per audit ($75), which is paid before cash arrives and so conflicts with the 'no up-front capital' limit (exposure cap $0) unless that cost is deferred. This does not change the stance.
